To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients with PTDM have a higher ratio of α(4)(7)β(7)+ to CLA+ regulatory T cells (CD4+CD25highCD127lowFOXP3+) at the time of hematopoietic cell transplant engraftment, which may be associated with an increased risk of PTDM.
PTDM is associated in a multivariate analysis with decreased frequencies of circulating CLA+ (skin-homing Tregs) and increased ratios of gut-homing to skin-homing Tregs after HSCT.
new-onset PTMD is associated with measurable alterations in Treg phenotype after allogeneiic hematopoietiic stem cell transplantation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel therapeutic intervention that could potentially reduce PTDM and improve long-term outcomes of HSCT.
the development of new therapies that can prevent or treat posttransplantation metabolic disorders such as posttransplantation hyperglycemia and diabetes mellitus.

the study of the immunological mechanisms that regulate immune tolerance and how these mechanisms can be modulated to prevent or treat diseases such as diabetes mellitus and graft versus host disease (GVHD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the frequency and function of Tregs are altered in patients with new-onsett diabetes mellitus after hematopoietic cell transplantation.

the results of the present study indicate that the frequency of circulating CD4(+)CD25(+)FoxP3(+) T cells in patients with PTDM was significantly lower at engrafting compared with that in the patients without PTDM.
the presence of a T cell population with a specific phenotype, which is able to inhibit the immune response against alloantigens, may be a key factor in the prevention of PTDM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the development of post-transplant diabetes after allogenechic stem cell transplantation is associated with a decreased frequency of circulating CLAs+ Tregs and an increased frequency of α4b7+ Tregs at the time of engraftment.
the development of new onset diabetes after transplantation is associated with altered regulatory T-cell phenotype after allogeneically hematopoietic cell transplantation.
the presence of PTDM is associated, after HSCT, with an increased ratio of gut-homing to skin-homing regulatory T cells (α(4)β7(+) to CLA(+)).
The main takeaway from our work is that
PTDM is associated in HSCT with a measurable change in Treg phenotype, and that the frequency of CLA(+) and α(4) β(7)(+) regulatory T cells (CD4(+)FoxP3(+)) is altered in PTDM.

PTDM is associated not only with decreased numbers of Tregs but also with a shift in Treg phenotype toward a gut-homing phenotype, which may contribute to the development of insulin resistance and PTDM.
PTDM is associated in part with changes in the Treg compartment.
